components.css: .ds-strip { display: flex; align-items: stretch; min-height: 60px; font-family: 'Be Vietnam Pro', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-strip.is-warning { background: var(--reflect, #c8201a); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--reflect-ink, #a81a15); } .ds-strip-label, .ds-strip-message { display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 20px; } .ds-strip-label { padding-left: 24px; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.2; white-space: nowrap; color: #fff; } .ds-strip-message { background: #fff; color: var(--reflect-ink, #a81a15); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-tape { flex: 1; position: relative; overflow: hidden; } .ds-tape-run { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--reflect, #c8201a) 0 56px, #fff 56px 112px); animation: ds-tape-in 420ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both; } .ds-strip-ack { align-self: center; margin: 0 24px 0 16px; min-height: 38px; padding: 7px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--ink, #16181b); border-radius: 4px; background: var(--ink, #16181b); color: #fff; font: inherit; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; } .ds-strip-ack:hover { background: #000; } .ds-strip-ack:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ink, #16181b); outline-offset: 2px; } @keyframes ds-tape-in { from { clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0); } to { clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-tape-run { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The screen is painted like the school bus it is watching. A yellow livery band carries the plate and the connection lights, a full-width reflective strip below it carries the safety state, the camera sits in a dark rounded window like the bus's own glass, and everything else is light grey painted steel with flat white panels riveted on by 1px lines. The world is industrial and plain: one sans family, tabular numbers, small corners, no shadows. Colour is paint and signal, never decoration.

Density is that of an operations desk, not a marketing page: a working grid that fills a laptop or a wall screen, compact 13–15px text, and three or four facts per panel. Calm is the default. When the bus is fine the strip is white with a green label; when a passenger may be left on board, the strip turns reflector red edge to edge with white-and-red tape, and nothing else on the page competes with it.

The world explicitly rejects the generic monitoring dashboard: equal-weight metric cards, a dark side navigation and a blue accent. Hierarchy comes from the bus metaphor (livery, strip, window, cabin plan) and from state, not from card grids.
keyCharacteristics: Yellow livery band on top, grey steel desk below, white panels with 1px rules.
A full-width reflective strip whose single state colour owns the whole band.
The camera framed in a dark "glass" window with a three-fact readout column.
A top-down cabin plan drawn only in 90° and 45° lines, sensors lit by real state.
One family (Be Vietnam Pro), tabular figures for every number.
Flat surfaces; depth only from the dark glass against light steel.

rules.name: The Livery Bar Rule
rules.body: Livery yellow fills the top bar and nothing larger than a marker. It never fills a panel, a card, a button or the strip.

rules.name: The One State Owns the Strip Rule
rules.body: The reflective strip shows exactly one state colour at a time, across the full width. Red is WARNING, amber is CHECK, green text on white is NORMAL, steel grey is OFFLINE or loading.

rules.name: The Signal Is Bound to State Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and green only appear when a real reading puts them there. Each signal colour has a fill and a darker ink/edge partner; use the ink partner for text on light grounds.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Be Vietnam Pro only, weights 400–700. No display face, no monospace.

rules.name: The Tabular Number Rule
rules.body: Every count, clock time, percentage and timestamp uses tabular figures so values never jitter as they update each second.

rules.name: The Strip Speaks Loudest Rule
rules.body: The strip label is the largest text on the desk. Nothing else may be set larger than 22px.

rules.name: The Flat Steel Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, glows or blurs. Separation comes from 1px rules, steel-versus-white grounds and the dark glass.

rules.name: The Only the Window Is Round Rule
rules.body: Nothing but the camera glass goes above 6px radius.

dos: **Do** let the reflective strip carry the safety state across the full width, one colour at a time, with the label at 22px (26px in WARNING).
**Do** pair every signal colour with words: markers carry a label and detail line, the legend explains each fill, the strip says the state in text.
**Do** show source and freshness next to every reading ("vừa xong", "12 giây trước"), and make stale data look stale: greyscale and dim the frame, drop readouts to Glass Muted, say "hết hiệu lực".
**Do** set every number in tabular figures.
**Do** draw the cabin plan in 90° and 45° lines only, and swap to the vertical drawing at ≤720px.
**Do** keep remote-control buttons in equal pairs and disable them, with a reason, when the board is offline.
donts: **Don't** fill panels, buttons or the strip with Livery Yellow; it belongs to the top bar and to small "person seen" marks.
**Don't** build equal-weight metric cards, a dark side navigation or a blue accent; this world rejects the generic dashboard.
**Don't** add drop shadows or glows to panels; depth is the dark glass against light steel.
**Don't** use red, amber or green as decoration; they appear only when a real reading puts them there.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or set anything larger than the strip label.
**Don't** remove a sent command from the list; change its state instead.
**Don't** round anything beyond 6px except the camera glass (10px).
